topic: Corporate Rebels 1-60 · low employee engagement statistics (6/6)

passage.text: Worldwide, only 15 percent of employees feel engaged with their work, which means that the majority is disengaged every day. Within this group, some employees are so frustrated that they actively try to damage their workplace. These workers make up 18 percent of the workforce. Studies in the Netherlands have shown that just one in ten employees is involved and engaged. These statistics place the majority of people, including friends, neighbours, and relatives, among those who are unhappy at work.

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Most employees worldwide are disengaged from work, with some actively harmful to their workplace.
wrong: Fifteen percent of employees damage their workplace through frustration.
The Netherlands has higher employee engagement than other countries.
taps.explain: The text emphasizes widespread disengagement as the main problem.

taps.context: These statistics place the majority of people, including friends, neighbours, and relatives, among those who are unhappy at work.
taps.correct: Most people you know are unhappy at their jobs.
wrong: Friends, neighbours, and relatives are never happy at work.
Statistics show that only a small group of people are unhappy at work.
taps.explain: The original uses examples to show how widespread workplace unhappiness is.
